frontier.hypothesis: Inline-expression form for p in both call sites (no local `p` binding, expression written directly in call arg) generates two distinct RTL pseudos, and would land p1's dest in v0.
frontier.mechanism: expand computes a fresh anonymous SI pseudo for each `((s16*)(offset+table))[N]` in a call arg, since there is no DECL_RTL of p to unify them. CSE MIGHT re-unify them into one pseudo, or MIGHT leave them separate since prev_idx vs next_idx differ. If separate, p1 addu emits `addu $newpseudo_p1, ...` where $newpseudo_p1 is local-alloc-eligible (single-BB single-def) and can land in v0.

frontier.hypothesis: Global.c's `expand_preferences` propagation for a PLUS SET picks up exactly ONE of the two operand hard regs into the dest's copy-prefs, following a specific first-src / dead-src heuristic that a directed C-source spelling can toggle.
frontier.mechanism: The greg data shows 86 pref is {3} only, coming from 129 (src1 of p2's addu at insn 124). Neither 130's a0 nor either p1 operand appears. Reading gcc-2.7.2/global.c will name the specific propagation code; a source-side lever (e.g. swapping which side of `+` holds the shifted offset vs the table pointer, or nudging pseudo lifetime so 130 has the propagated slot) may redirect the copy-pref away from v1.

If pref-3 disappears in favor of pref-4 (a0), 86 could still land in v1 (via conflict avoidance) but with no positive bias — a second lever might then move it to v0.
